_comment: Versioned registry of REVIEWED additions to the GDELT news allowlist (sources/gdelt.py TRUSTED_DOMAINS). It mirrors the admission discipline of reviewed_feeds.json: an entry is a reviewed claim with a standing, a reviewer and a date, never a scraped guess. A domain being public is not enough; each entry says WHY the outlet is national press of record, a wire, a public broadcaster, the business press, or the regional daily of an industrial region where collective dismissals are reported first. Review evidence, 2026-09-02 (Claude review pass, offline): NO outlet page, robots.txt or feed was fetched, by rule; standing is argued from what each publication is, and every domain was checked against the refusal ledger in railway/country_coverage.py (REFUSAL_LEDGER), which tests/test_reviewed_outlets.py re-checks on every run. Merging the change that adds a domain here is the owner's approval of that claim. Additive only: existing allowlist entries are never removed or reordered from here. Second pass, 2026-09-03 (Claude review pass, offline, no fetch): the 2026-09-02 run's own health detail measured Italy 4.2%, UK 5.4% and Germany 8.5% kept/seen against Spain's 22.4% the SAME day its outlets landed, proof the allowlist is the binding constraint outside the anglophone press. Triggered by a concrete miss: 'DNB schrapt 290 banen' (De Nederlandsche Bank, 290 jobs), carried by two unlisted Dutch outlets while the Netherlands admitted only 3. `reviewed_at`/`reviewer` below now describe the LATEST pass; entries carry no per-entry date, so a reader wanting which pass added a given domain should cross-reference the dated BEGIN/END block in sources/gdelt.py that names it.
reviewer: Claude review pass, offline, no fetch

outlets.standing: Spain's state-owned national news agency, founded 1939, and the largest Spanish-language wire. Its economy desk files every ERE (expediente de regulacion de empleo) announcement and the national and regional dailies syndicate it, so admitting the wire admits the report at its origin rather than one outlet's rewrite.
outlets.caveat: State-owned. The exact host GDELT records for its articles was not checked; efe.com is the agency's own public site.

outlets.standing: The largest private news agency in Spain. Its economy service is the highest-volume reporter of ERE filings and works-council negotiations, and it is syndicated by national and regional titles alike, which is why a Spanish layoff usually appears here first.
The statutory public broadcaster (Corporacion RTVE), with a national news operation whose economy desk reports collective dismissals nationwide.
National daily of record founded 1903 (Vocento). With El Pais, El Mundo and La Razon it is one of Spain's four national general dailies; the other three were already listed or are added here.

The fourth of Spain's national general dailies (Grupo Planeta), with an economy section that carries ERE and restructuring coverage; listed so the national general press is complete rather than three-quarters present.
Spain's leading digital-native daily, with a companies desk that regularly breaks restructuring and ERE news before the print titles carry it.
Among the largest Spanish news sites by audience. Its business supplement Invertia (invertia.elespanol.com, admitted by this suffix) reports corporate restructuring and listed-company workforce cuts.
Major independent digital daily with a dedicated economy and labour desk, among the most-read Spanish news sites.
outlets.caveat: Editorially left of centre; balances ABC and La Razon. The extractor judges the article text, not the outlet's line.

outlets.standing: Prensa Iberica's flagship daily in Barcelona. Catalonia is Spain's largest industrial region (automotive, chemicals, pharma) and its plant closures and EREs are reported here first.

The largest regional daily in Spain by circulation. Galicia's automotive cluster around Vigo and its shipyards are among the country's most ERE-prone employers, and their cuts run here before the Madrid titles.

The Basque Country's leading daily (Vocento, Bilbao). The Basque industrial belt of steel, machine tools and automotive components produces a steady flow of collective-dismissal reporting that is local news first.
The public broadcaster's news service (France Televisions with Radio France), national news with a full economy desk that reports plans sociaux (PSE) and plant closures.
outlets.caveat: A migration to franceinfo.fr has been announced by the broadcaster; only the long-standing host is listed, because the new one could not be verified without fetching.

outlets.standing: France's leading 24-hour news channel and, through BFM Business on the same host, its leading business channel. Its economy desk covers PSE announcements and restructurings daily.
The largest-circulation daily in France, regional in base and national in reach. Industrial closures in the west (agri-food, automotive, shipbuilding) are reported here first and often only here.
National daily (the Aujourd'hui en France edition is distributed nationwide) with an economy desk that reports restructurings across the Paris region, France's largest employment basin.
National daily (Bayard), one of France's national general dailies, with regular labour and social-affairs reporting on collective redundancies.
Leading national newsmagazine whose site carries the AFP economy wire in full, so a PSE dispatch appears here even when the print dailies pass on it.
The leading French business weekly; corporate restructuring, closures and headcount reductions are its core beat.
Business monthly (Prisma Media) whose site is one of the highest-volume French economy news sites, wire-backed, and reports layoffs at named employers daily.

The industrial trade weekly of record, published since 1891. It reports factory-level PSEs and closures plant by plant, most of which never reach the national dailies; for a layoff tracker it is the single highest-value French title.

Public international broadcaster (France Medias Monde, sister of the already listed france24.com), with French-language economy reporting on France and on francophone Africa, where the regional feeds are thin.
Leading daily of Hauts-de-France, the region carrying the largest share of French automotive and steel employment, where plant cuts are reported locally days before any national title.

The national news agency and the wire behind most Turkish reporting; company and factory news is filed here first and syndicated by every national and regional title. The repo's own Turkey market table already names Anadolu.
outlets.caveat: State-owned. Balanced by Sozcu, T24 and Evrensel below.

outlets.standing: News channel and site of the statutory public broadcaster TRT. Its provincial bureaus report factory closures and regional dismissals, and ministry statements on collective layoffs are carried here in full, which makes it the public-service counterpart of the state wire.
The leading Turkish business and finance channel; listed-company news and corporate restructuring are its core beat. Named in the repo's Turkey market table.

Turkey's business daily of record, Dunya Gazetesi, which moved its site to ekonomim.com. The already listed dunya.com is the old host, kept because nothing is removed from here; the repo's Turkey market table and source catalogue already name Ekonomim.
outlets.caveat: Whether dunya.com still resolves or redirects was not checked.

outlets.standing: The largest mainstream national daily. Only its English edition (hurriyetdailynews.com) was listed, so its Turkish-language reporting, where the plant-level detail is, was never admitted.
Major national news channel and site with a strong economy desk that reports named-employer workforce cuts.
The highest-circulation opposition daily and among the top two Turkish papers overall; carries dismissals that government-aligned titles underplay. Named in the repo's Turkey market table.
outlets.caveat: Opposition-aligned; balances the state and pro-government entries.

outlets.standing: Leading independent digital newspaper, one of the most-read news sites in Turkey and named in the repo's own Turkey market table; it carries dismissal reporting that the government-aligned print titles pass on.

A national daily whose beat is labour: plant-level dismissals and union disputes are its lead stories, which is exactly the reporting a layoff tracker needs and the reporting other titles carry least.
outlets.caveat: Left-wing and union-aligned. The count and employer are read from the article text and judged by the extractor, not taken from the outlet's framing.

outlets.standing: The largest private domestic news agency, with regional bureaus that report factory closures in Bursa, Kocaeli and Izmir before the national desks pick them up.

The Dutch public broadcaster's news service, the country's most-cited general news source; its business desk covers collective dismissals and works-council notifications nationwide, and it is the outlet the 2026-09-03 DNB miss (290 jobs, De Nederlandsche Bank) named as absent.
Among the highest-traffic Dutch news sites, wire-backed (ANP) rolling news with an economy section; the second outlet the 2026-09-03 DNB miss named as absent from the allowlist.
The largest-circulation Dutch daily (DPG Media), with a dedicated economy section (Telegraaf Financieel) that reports corporate restructuring and job cuts.
National daily of record (DPG Media) with regular labour and social-affairs coverage of collective dismissals.
One of the largest Dutch dailies by readership (DPG Media), with regional business desks that report plant-level cuts before the national titles do.
The Netherlands' leading commercial broadcaster's news service, with an economy desk (RTL Z content runs here) that reports named-employer workforce cuts daily.

The Netherlands' only dedicated business and financial news radio station; corporate restructuring and layoffs are its core beat, comparable to the role Bloomberg HT plays for Turkey in this registry.

Algemeen Nederlands Persbureau, the Dutch national news agency; its economy wire is syndicated by nearly every Dutch title (NU.nl included), so admitting it admits Dutch layoff reports at their point of origin.

Italy's largest and oldest news agency (a cooperative of the major publishers), the wire behind most Italian corporate and labour reporting; company and factory news is filed here first and syndicated nationwide.
outlets.caveat: Standing verified as a publisher's cooperative, not state-owned; distinct from the state broadcaster RAI also added here.

outlets.standing: The news service of Italy's statutory public broadcaster (RAI), with a national economy desk that reports collective dismissals and plant closures.
outlets.caveat: State broadcaster; balanced by ANSA (publisher cooperative) and the independent dailies already listed.

outlets.standing: A major independent national daily with a dedicated economy desk that regularly covers corporate restructuring, distinct editorially from the four already-listed titles.
Rome's paper of record and among Italy's highest-circulation dailies, with an economy section covering the capital region's large public and private employers.
A financial daily focused on listed companies and corporate news, complementing Il Sole 24 Ore's broader business coverage the way Expansion complements El Pais for Spain in this registry.
A leading German 24-hour news channel with a strong business desk (RTL Group); named-employer restructuring and workforce cuts are reported here daily.
Germany's leading business weekly (Handelsblatt Media Group); corporate restructuring, closures and headcount reductions are its core beat.
A leading German business monthly (Spiegel Group) that reports executive and corporate decisions, including restructuring and layoffs, at named companies.
Berlin's national daily of record, with a business section covering the capital region's large employers and federal-level economic policy affecting collective dismissals.

The leading daily of North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany's most populous state and its largest industrial employment base (steel, chemicals, automotive supply); plant-level cuts are reported here first, the same role La Voix du Nord plays for France in this registry.

The UK's highest-reach news site by audience (DMG Media); its business desk covers major-employer layoffs, and admitting it closes a gap where the Times, Telegraph and Guardian were already listed but the single largest UK news readership was not.
outlets.caveat: Tabloid editorial style; the extractor judges the article text for facts, not the outlet's framing.

outlets.standing: The news service of the UK's leading commercial public-service broadcaster, with regional bureaus that report factory and office closures across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
A statutory public-service broadcaster's national news operation, distinct editorially from the BBC and ITV already listed, with regular business and economy coverage.
